references.text: The cloud covered Mount Sinai when God descended upon it, just as here in chapter 24. Both texts describe God's presence manifested through the cloud on the mountain.
Moses was called up the mountain by the Lord, and this verse continues the narrative of his ascent to the mountain.
The Lord came down in the cloud and stood with Moses on the mountain, showing the same pattern of God's presence in the cloud on the mountain.
The cloud covered the tabernacle, just as the cloud covered the mountain. God's presence is manifested through the cloud in both places.
The cloud filled the Lord's house when the temple was dedicated, just as the cloud covered the mountain as a sign of God's glory and presence.
At Jesus' transfiguration on the mountain, a bright cloud came and overshadowed the disciples, reflecting God's presence in the cloud at Sinai.
A cloud came and overshadowed the disciples on the Mount of Transfiguration, parallel to the cloud that covered Mount Sinai when Moses went up.
The Psalms use the cloud motif from the Sinai account as a theological image of God's majestic presence.
Repetition of the same theological image from Sinai in another psalm.
Complementary events that together show the consequence of meeting God in the cloud.
The cloud, as a sign of God's presence, moves from Mount Sinai to the tent of meeting.
